query: Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets provide 16 candidate alloys, nine of which are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing. Early reports associated increasing constituent count with greater strength, but that simple relationship is no longer generally accepted. Despite extensive experimental and theoretical investigation, the origins of differences in deformation and failure behavior remain unresolved; practical interpretation must also account for constituent cost and overall cost-performance balance. What testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs these mechanical-property differences and why? Define a controlled investigation, the observations predicted relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline, the limits within which the hypothesis should apply, the prior evidence supporting it, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Variations in constituent composition in FCC high-entropy alloys alter local lattice distortions that modulate the stacking fault energy (SFE) distribution, thereby shifting the dominant deformation mechanisms (twinning versus dislocation glide), which in turn governs the mechanical-property differences observed across equiatomic, quaternary, and ternary alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni high-entropy alloy processed to form a single-phase FCC structure.
generation.intervention: Prepare quaternary and ternary subsets by selectively reducing or substituting specific constituent elements (e.g., varying Mn or Co content) while maintaining the overall FCC structure.
generation.conditions: Maintain uniform thermomechanical processing and impurity control for all compositions; conduct mechanical testing at room temperature and at elevated temperatures to evaluate temperature effects.
generation.structural_mediator: Local lattice distortions influencing the stacking fault energy (SFE) distribution.
generation.mechanism: Elemental substitutions change atomic size mismatches and electronic environments, which modifies the local lattice distortions and hence the SFE. Lower SFE values favor the activation of deformation twinning and higher strain hardening, while higher SFE promotes dislocation glide, ultimately leading to the observed differences in yield strength and failure modes.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the equiatomic quinary baseline, alloys with modified compositions that result in a lower effective SFE will exhibit increased twinning activity and enhanced strain-hardening behavior (thereby showing higher yield strength), while those with a higher effective SFE will show reduced twinning and more conventional dislocation glide leading to lower yield strength.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to FCC single-phase high-entropy alloys produced under similar thermomechanical conditions; it may not hold in alloys that develop secondary phases or under processing conditions that alter the FCC stability.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative contribution of SFE alterations on mechanical strength is uncertain, and additional factors such as elemental clustering or segregation might also significantly influence deformation behavior.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize the equiatomic quinary baseline and a series of quaternary and ternary alloys with intentional variation in elements controlling SFE (e.g., through adjustments in Mn and Co levels). Conduct standardized thermomechanical processing and then perform mechanical testing (e.g., tensile tests) combined with in-situ microstructural investigations (using TEM or digital image correlation) to monitor deformation mechanisms. Independently estimate the SFE either experimentally (if feasible) or through ab initio calculations.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloys predicted to have a lower SFE do not consistently display increased twinning activity and enhanced strain hardening relative to the equiatomic baseline, or if no systematic correlation is observed between the measured SFE values and dominant deformation mechanisms, the mechanistic hypothesis would be falsified.
